decision: Finder selects the dungeon and roster. Humans walk to the entrance and manually enter; NPCs join the party dungeon automatically. Ordinary party invitations never teleport. No second group-wide entry confirmation.
scope: Matched-roster authorization and per-human manual intentions checked within existing sealed-room transfer transaction. Complete runtime/asset pipeline exercised with two humans and three NPCs, using MemoryStore and PGlite.

tests.goldenScenarios: All five complete state/RNG/reward samples unchanged

verified: Matching acceptance creates a dungeon/roster record with zero human manual-entry requests
Ordinary invitation, timed-out proposal or forged account cannot substitute a human entry request
Membership, leader, role, source controller accounts, level and target dungeon are checked at the transaction boundary
Current whole-room composition rejects until every included human has requested entry
Human source locations still pass the ordinary entrance rules; no human location rewrite or return-point teleport metadata remains
NPC runtime members can start in another world location and enter the dungeon without manual requests
Group instance binding, all twenty-two identity claims and checkpoint transfer commit or roll back together
Duplicate transfer, original-owner fencing, normal target recovery and private participant presentations
No additional tables, external queue or per-tick database operations
limitations: Public entry orchestration and gateway/browser routing are not connected; autoTeleport remains false
First human entry with NPCs and later incremental human arrivals are the target but not yet implemented
Current whole-room composition requires all five prepared seats and all human entrance locations together
NPC roster selection/bench removal and member departure remain incomplete
PGlite validates SQL transactions here; not a real PostgreSQL multi-connection fault or capacity test
No browser, complete shared encounter or loot distribution acceptance this turn
